desc:
The reflected binary Gray code of an integer i is g(i) = i ^ (i >> 1). Consecutive codes g(0), g(1), g(2), ... differ in exactly one bit.

For a given k, consider the k steps from g(i-1) to g(i) for i = 1, 2, ..., k. Each step flips exactly one bit; number the positions from 0 for the least significant bit. Return the sum of the flipped positions over these steps.

k = 0 -> 0   (no steps)
k = 1 -> 0   (0 to 1 flips bit 0)
k = 2 -> 1   (the steps flip bits 0 and 1)
k = 4 -> 3   (the steps flip bits 0, 1, 0 and 2)
hints: Write out g(0) to g(8) and look at which bit changes at each step.
The bit that changes when moving to g(i) is the lowest set bit of i, so its position is the number of trailing zeros of i.
Sum the trailing zero counts: for each j ≥ 1, the number of i in 1..k divisible by 2j is k // 2j. Add these counts up.
editorial: Going from g(i-1) to g(i) flips the bit at position t, where 2t is the lowest set bit of i. A short check on small values confirms this, and it is why the Gray sequence is called a reflected code: the flips follow the ruler sequence 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 1, 0, 3, ...

Instead of adding the positions one at a time, count contributions by level. Position t is credited once for every i that is a multiple of 2t, and adding the credits for t = 1, 2, ... gives the answer, since sum of ctz(i) = sum over j ≥ 1 of floor(k / 2j). The loop runs about log2 k times.
solution:
def grayFlipSum(k):
    total = 0
    p = 2
    while p <= k:
        total += k // p
        p *= 2
    return total
